Subject: Evergreen — MAP proposal and legal sequencing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team found the latency and cost breakdown very helpful. We want to move toward an evaluation MAP and understand the procurement/legal cadence so we can align our IT security review, procurement approvals, and the signature window for the MSA/DPA/order form.

High level asks from our side:
- 8–10 week pilot evaluation window with a clear acceptance test (throughput & PII handling).
- Confirmation of which MSA clauses Redwood needs to keep as-is vs. negotiable (data residency, subprocessing, audit).
- A sequencing proposal showing parallel vs. serial items (evidence collection vs. legal redlines).

I attached a simple intake sheet with our preferred gates. Can you propose a MAP that maps Redwood deliverables to our procurement checkpoints? Hoping to get legal engaged early so we don't hit last-minute delays.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Sourcing, Evergreen Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Evergreen — MAP proposal and legal sequencing

Sophie — thanks for the clear asks and the intake sheet. I pulled together a draft MAP and sequencing recommendation and attached it (Evergreen_MAP_v1.xlsx). Summary below so it's easy to circulate to your procurement/legal teams:  

Proposed high-level structure (8 week pilot target):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & NDA sign (if needed) — Redwood to provide SOC2 report + dataflow diagram.
2) Weeks 1–2: Security evidence collection (our standard checklist) runs in parallel with legal review of MSA/DPA redlines.
3) Weeks 3–5: Pilot test window (integration, sample dataset, performance run). Acceptance criteria defined in sheet (latency percentiles, anomaly rate, and specific PII handling checks).
4) Week 6: Acceptance review & remediation cycle (if needed).
5) Week 7: Order form finalization (SOW, usage caps, billing cadence).
6) Week 8: Signatures and onboarding handoff (CS/Eng runbook).

Key sequencing notes:
- Security evidence (SOC2, penetration test summary, KMS/HSM docs) should be delivered in Week 1–2 to unblock internal IT. This is parallel to MSA redline review. In many cases procurement will not sign off until evidence is confirmed, so treating those as concurrent reduces overall time.
- We recommend a focused redline pass from Evergreen Legal limited to mandatory clauses (data residency, breach notification timing, indemnity cap). Everything else we can defer to the order form or a later amendment to speed signature.
- If Evergreen requires a formal DPA sign-off before pilot, we can provide a DPA template and a tracked change PDF — we highlighted the few high-risk items in the attached PDF.

Next actions I propose:
- Karthik (legal) to review the attached MSA redlines and flag any non-negotiables.
- Ben (solutions) to own pilot success criteria and provide a short test plan we can embed in the MAP.
- Sophie/Evergreen to confirm procurement's absolute no-go items (e.g., local hosting requirement).

I attached: Evergreen_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), Redwood_MSA_redlines_20260506.pdf (redline + comments), evidence-checklist-security.xlsx (what we'll provide).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 13:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evergreen — MAP proposal and legal sequencing

Looping in Laura from Contracts & Ops for the order form workflow. Quick notes from legal review (initial pass):
- Data residency: Evergreen's ask for EU-only residency would be a blocker; for US-based customers we can commit to region-specific routing and audit logs but not exclusive regional tenancy without Dedicated placement. Identify whether this is a firm requirement.
- Indemnity/limitation language: proposed modest edits to align with our standard liability cap (1x ARR for pilot to be scoped in OF).
- Audit rights: provide SOC2 + summary of third-party audits; if Evergreen requires full audit rights we need to scope and price that separately.

Sequencing recommendation from legal:
- Accept pilot evidence + SOC2 (Week 1–2) -> begin pilot.
- While pilot is running, perform redline negotiation (Weeks 3–5). This means signatures could converge at Week 7 assuming order form is ready.

I'll add inline comments in the redline PDF. If Evergreen insists on different sequencing (e.g., legal sign first) we should get a clear procurement rationale so we can propose compensating controls (short-term escrow, enhanced logging).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marissa and Karthik — this is very helpful and reads like a practical path forward. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/IT: 

- Evergreen can accept the pilot starting with SOC2 + evidence package; that will let IT start the integration work.
- On data residency: Evergreen's security team prefers regional guarantees but for this pilot they can accept routing + audit logs. We will confirm whether Dedicated is a longer-term ask in our internal steering meeting next Wednesday.
- Procurement would like the order form template completed by Week 6 to avoid last-minute billing surprises. Can your ops team commit to a Week 6 OF draft?

We will book a 30-minute alignment call for next Tuesday to walk the MAP together and get legal/procurement alignment. Sending calendar invite.

Sophie
Sophie Lang
